title: Deployment Weeksmith: schedule, staffing tactics & release brief (Jul 2026) - sketch
content:
Purpose: compact play-notes for a condensed 5-day deploy cycle ("weeksmith"). This doc mixes a lightweight schedule, shift/staffing tactics, a short checklist for preflight + cutover, and a first-cut release-notes draft. Use as a running scratchpad for the next sprint deploy (target week: 2026-07-12).

Summary bullets:
- Goal: ship v2026.7.12 with model-routing improvements + batching heuristic tweak; preserve <150ms p95 latency for hot routes.
- Risk profile: medium (non-breaking infra change; potential traffic skew from routing). Canary required across 3 regions.
- Operational objective: no customer-visible errors; telemetry drift <3% for token cost.

Weeksmith schedule (compact):
- Day -3 (Wed): final readiness sync; QA signoff; telemetry smoke harness run.
- Day -1 (Fri): production config baked; canary manifests pre-applied in staging; comms note sent 09:00 PT.
- Day 0 (Mon 07:00 PT): small-batch canary start (0.5% traffic) -> monitor 90m -> increase to 5% if green -> 30% after 2h -> full ramp by 6h with staged region handoff.
- Day +1: stabilize and sample logs; validate fallback policies.
- Day +2: post-release evaluation; capture lessons & update rollforward doc.

Staffing & handoff tactics:
- On-call steward: primary owner for cutover (Marco). Escalation: SRE L2 (Elaine) then infra lead (Connor).
- Overlap window: ensure 2hr overlap between US and EU ops handoffs.
- Nightwatch: minimal guard crew 22:00-02:00 PT for first 48h.
- Quick-contacts: #release-weeksmith Slack channel; pager duty rotation assigned.

Preflight checklist (short):
- [ ] Config freeze (no unrelated PR merges after Day -2 17:00 PT)
- [ ] Smoke harness passes (latency + error budget) in staging
- [ ] Canary manifests validated for region affinity
- [ ] DB migration: none (confirm) / if present, migration dry-run done
- [ ] Observability: dashboards published, baseline snapshots captured
- [ ] Rollback artifact: tested rollback job and canary policy defined
- [ ] Customer comms drafted + legal review if needed

Cutover signals & thresholds (fast heuristics):
- Immediate rollback if: error rate spike > 0.5% absolute or latency p95 upstream > 250ms for 3 consecutive 5-min buckets.
- Slowdown and hold at current percentage if: token-cost increase > 10% above baseline or throughput drop > 15%.
- Proceed to next stage only after 30m of stable trends and no alerts.

Telemetry sampling plan:
- Pull baseline from last 7 days for hot routes (top 20 endpoints).
- Add synthetic load-run at each ramp step (5m) to validate KV cache behavior.
- Sample 1% of full payloads for content-regression checks (privacy-safe).

Release notes (draft):
- Title: v2026.7.12 — smarter routing and batch tuning
- Highlights: improved routing policy to reduce cross-AZ hops; adaptive batching reduces tail tokens for short prompts; improved monitoring for prefix cache health.
- Impact: transparent to end users; expect 3–7% lower per-token cost for chat workloads; no API contract changes.
- Known issues: rare metric undercount seen on staging for large payloads (investigating).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who will own the customer debrief for enterprise accounts that saw higher token-cost during the last patch? (assign before Day -1)
- Confirm KMS key rotation window doesn't collide with cutover—security to confirm.
- Validate third-party metrics exporter for EU region; flaky in last run.

Post-release capture (to-do immediately after Day +2):
- Short retro (30m) with stakeholders: what went well, what surprised us, what to automate next time.
- Update the permanent release-runbook with any new thresholds or new smoke tests.
- Convert Slack timeline into a concise incident/ops log for audit.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep rollforward tiny: prefer hotfix micro-deploys over wide rollforwards.
- If canary shows token-cost regressions but latency OK, prefer staged config rollback (routing percentage) rather than code rollback.
- Keep comms plain: "no action required; monitoring active" unless rollback triggered.

References and quick links (working):
- Canary dashboard: dashboards/redwood/canary-weeksmith (placeholder)
- Pager rota: https://oncall.redwood.com/rota/weeksmith

End of sketch — edit in-place as we lock calendar.
